'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that [[New York (state)|New York]] is expected to move into phase four of its reopening plan. However, indoor public spaces will remain closed. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/no-new-indoor-activities-in-nyc-in-phase-4-cuomo-says-2020-07-16 (MarketWatch)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas]]
****[[List of governors of Arkansas|Arkansas Governor]] [[Asa Hutchinson]] announces that masks will be made mandatory in public spaces. The order is expected to go into effect on July 20. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/507713-arkansas-governor-issues-statewide-mask-mandate (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****[[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade County]] is expected to give people who violate COVID-19 guidelines a $100 fine. [https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/local/people-not-wearing-masks-can-get-100-fine-in-miami-dade-county/2263555/?amp (WTVJ)]
***The [[Centers for Disease Control]] extends the [[United States]] ban on cruise ships to September 30, citing ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships|COVID-19 cruise ship outbreaks]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/cdc-extends-us-ban-cruise-ships-september-71829608 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
***[[Spain]] honors their [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] victims at the [[Royal Palace of Madrid]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain-tribute-idUSKCN24H1E6 (Reuters)]
***Spain reports their highest COVID-19 infection count since May 10, with 580 cases. These cases have increased in the regions of [[Aragon]] and [[Catalonia]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/07/16/world/europe/16reuters-health-coronavirus-spain-catalonia.html?searchResultPosition=5 (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] surpasses two million cases. The death toll reaches 76,000. [https://apnews.com/1b4263980a7e4afde43be1d7cba82fde (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
***[[Reuters]] reports that the occupation of [[geisha]] in [[Tokyo]] is threatened by the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]], with awkward working conditions and the absence of new [[Geisha#Stages of training|apprentices]]. [https://widerimage.reuters.com/story/itll-take-all-of-our-body-and-soul-geisha-struggle-to-survive-in-the-shadow-of-coronavirus (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Censorship of Facebook]]
**[[Samoan Prime Minister]] [[Tuilaepa Aiono Sailele Malielegaoi]] says his country is "looking seriously at banning [[Facebook]] in the country" after "many people complained how it is used to hurt people", being himself a target of "defamation". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/421311/samoa-govt-looking-to-ban-facebook (RNZ)]
*[[George Floyd protests]], [[George Floyd protests in Oregon]]
**[[Kate Brown]], governor of [[Oregon]], criticizes President [[Donald Trump]] and acting Secretary of Homeland Security [[Chad Wolf]] amid reports of federal agents detaining protesters in [[Portland, Oregon]], the most populous city in the state. Wolf tweeted the previous day that the forces were sent to the city due to it being "under siege for 47 straight days by a violent mob." [https://thehill.com/blogs/blog-briefing-room/news/507841-oregon-governor-criticizes-trump-sending-federal-officers-to (''The Hill'')]
*In the [[United Kingdom]], the [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeal]] rules that 20-year-old British-born [[Shamima Begum]], who left the country to join [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] in 2015, can return to the UK to fight for her [[British nationality law|citizenship]] after the [[Home Office]] revoked it while she was living in a [[refugee camp]] in [[Syria]], due to her joining a terrorist group. The Home Office says the court's decision is "very disappointing" and that it would apply for permission to appeal. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-53427197 (BBC News)]
*The [[European Court of Justice]] issues a ruling invalidating the [[EU–US Privacy Shield]] framework that allows EU-to-US data transfers by companies. [https://www.cnet.com/news/us-eu-privacy-shield-data-sharing-pact-invalidated-over-surveillance-fears/ (c<nowiki>&#124;</nowiki>net)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 North Macedonian parliamentary election]]
**The [[Social Democratic Union of Macedonia]] is projected to win a [[Plurality (voting)|plurality]] of votes in [[North Macedonia]]'s latest election. The [[Macedonian nationalism|nationalist]] [[VMRO-DPMNE]] would come a close second. [https://www.dw.com/en/north-macedonia-elections-pro-eu-social-democrats-take-narrow-lead/a-54192639 (DW)]
*[[Politics of Gabon]]
**[[Rose Christiane Raponda]] becomes the first female [[Prime Minister of Gabon]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-07-16/gabon-names-first-woman-as-prime-minister-in-cabinet-reshuffle (Bloomberg)]
